repository.executionRule: Run one meal-grid pilot from a clean descendant containing A857 through A861. Freeze the bank, corpus, prompts, tools, model, topology, token limits and acceptance rules before the first answer is observed. A budget-only re-registration is allowed before execution when newly authorized compute exists; it must not alter semantic or retrieval settings.

execution.artifactDirectoryRule: Create a fresh directory containing the exact execution commit and UTC timestamp; never overwrite an earlier pilot.

budget.authorizationBasis: On 2026-09-28 the user added and authorized 5 USD of OpenAI API credit for the causal campaign. A868 through A870 exposed and corrected the OpenAI schema, canonical-title echo and noisy dossier handoff. A871 then spent 0.1830229 USD and returned a twenty-candidate inventory, but the inventory parser rejected two documentary titles split by OCR layout tokens even though the final identity validator already accepts those bounded patterns. Candidate Inventory now reuses the same bounded identity recognition for ignorable service tokens and page-marker title splits, with exact source and evidence constraints preserved. Corpus, bank, model, topology and acceptance rules remain frozen; this validation consistency change is the registered causal fix. Automatic purchase and automatic reload remain prohibited.

pilot: The one registered meal-grid case completes on the exact clean execution state with the sealed reference corpus unchanged.

The Candidate Explorer is present in the preflight seal with Responses transport, agent topology, workspace, 32768 history characters, a 4096-token Explorer output budget and seven total provider calls.
The Explorer dossier reaches the Writer with at least twenty distinct body-verified candidates and at least five candidates assigned by the model to each of the four requested meal roles.
Every retained candidate has an exact documentary title and at least one canonical body EvidenceId; locator-only contents or index excerpts do not satisfy body coverage.
The final result is answered with twenty concrete, distinct and semantically suitable selections, one for every weekday and meal moment, with canonical source references and no unsupported item.
The durable job, provider telemetry, tool events, candidate checkpoint, final claims and source payload are preserved for mechanical and human semantic review.
A precise bounded gap is safe behavior but fails this functional pilot when the historical corpus contains the missing bodies.
acceptance.progressionRule: Only a successful and semantically reviewed first pilot permits registration of repetitions two and three on the same frozen semantic configuration. Failure returns to causal trace review; it does not authorize prompt stacking or a larger budget by itself.
acceptance.productPromotionRule: Keep TESTE_NON_APPROUVE after this pilot. Product promotion still requires two further consecutive successes, a new blind holdout, durable end-to-end recovery and WinUI source-card validation.

stopRules: Do not execute while the persistent lifetime budget cannot reserve the first provider call.
Do not execute without a paid-tier observation less than 15 minutes old.
Stop before the first model call if the branch, clean-tree rule, bank hash, local router binary, model or provider configuration differs.
Stop before the first model call if the reference corpus cannot be sealed or has an active ingestion job; reject the pilot if the postflight seal differs.
Stop at the persistent lifetime, per-job or per-call guard; do not purchase or reload credits automatically.
Do not run repetitions two or three after a failed or semantically unreviewed first pilot.
